en.title: The most lucrative AI startup opportunities in 2027
en.summary: AI can churn out content at scale, yet many accounts end up sounding more and more alike: exposure without trust, topics without customers. The problem is often that they focus only on posting, without ever thinking through "why this person is worth following long-term." Doe Koe's latest article is worth a close read for creators.
en.reason: Goldman Sachs projects the creator economy will grow from $250 billion in 2023 to $480 billion in 2027, and creator ad revenue is expected to reach about $185 billion in 2025, surpassing traditional media for the first time, while Doe Koe argues that AI-generated content alone produces exposure without trust and explains why creators must build attention that converts into long-term audiences and customers.

items.title: Codex改了又测、测了又改，我一查Token才发现这个坑
items.summary: 让 Codex 修个小问题，它却“改—全量测—再改”。跑上半天，额度和耐心一起见底；更糟的是，一堆测试通过，真正点运行还是报错。作者给出一套可直接塞进 AGENTS.md 的收口办法。常用Codex、Claude Code却总被“自我循环”拖慢的人，可以照着改一次规则试一试。

items.recommend_reason_zh: 作者让 Codex 反复改代码再测试，结果发现反复分析和修改吃掉大量 Token，还举了已通过237272个测试、一运行却 Error xxx 无法启动的例子，并翻讨论看别人是否也遇到简单任务被塞满测试。

en.title: Codex edited then tested, tested then edited again—I only spotted the trap when I checked the Tokens
en.summary: Ask Codex to fix one small issue, and it cycles through edit, full test run, edit again. Half a day disappears, and your quota and patience hit bottom together. Worse: a pile of tests pass, but hitting run still throws an error. The author offers a set of guardrails you can drop straight into AGENTS.md. If you use Codex or Claude Code regularly and keep getting slowed down by these self-loops, it's worth adjusting your rules once and giving it a try.
en.reason: Codex can burn through tokens by repeatedly editing and running full test suites, as shown by a case where 237,272 tests passed yet the app failed to start with Error xxx, with AGENTS.md rules offered to stop that loop.

en.title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 enables stateless HTTP mode by default, adds multi-turn request support
en.summary:
Microsoft has officially released MCP C# SDK 2.0, implementing the 2026-07-28 revision of the MCP specification. The release refactors the HTTP layer around a stateless design and adds support for multi-round trip requests (MRTR) and dynamic capability negotiation.

The initialize handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header are gone: protocol version and capability declarations now travel with each request. Streamable HTTP servers are stateless by default, and HTTP request headers are standardized to simplify infrastructure routing. Legacy clients degrade gracefully, while state-related configuration and the traditional SSE endpoint trigger explicit warning codes (MCP9006/MCP9004).
en.reason: Microsoft's MCP C# SDK 2.0 implements the MCP 2026-07-28 revision, defaults Streamable HTTP servers to stateless, drops the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header, adds multi-round-trip requests (MRTR), and flags legacy stateful or SSE setups with MCP9006/MCP9004 warnings.

en.title: Google releases ML Drift to accelerate on-device AI inference across GPUs
en.summary:
Google launches ML Drift, an open-source cross-platform GPU compute engine for on-device AI and machine learning inference.

Word count: 1,240 words
Reading time: about 4 minutes

ML Drift is Google's open-source cross-platform GPU inference engine, built specifically for on-device AI. It unifies OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU behind a single abstraction and powers the LiteRT runtime.

It supports 5D tensors, tensor-virtualizing shaders and extensible custom operators; it is deeply optimized for Arm, Intel and Qualcomm GPUs; and it provides an inference foundation that balances the stability of traditional ML with the peak performance demanded by generative AI.

Intended for edge AI engineers, on-device inference framework developers and builders of heterogeneous computing runtimes.

Google has released ML Drift, an open-source, cross-platform GPU compute engine designed for on-device AI and machine learning inference. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it abstracts away the complexity of different GPU hardware and low-level APIs, supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU.

ML Drift is the core GPU acceleration engine powering LiteRT
en.reason: Google open-sourced ML Drift, an Apache 2.0 cross-platform GPU inference engine for on-device AI that unifies OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU, powers LiteRT, and cuts memory overhead 12% versus llama.cpp and MLX LM.

en.title: Anthropic adds optional security scanning service for critical open source projects
en.reason: Anthropic’s free, opt-in OSS Scanner uses Claude Mythos to send maintainers unreviewed reports with reproduction steps and candidate patches; in six months it flagged over 29,000 potential flaws, including a curl HTTP/2 upload use-after-free fixed in 8.23.0.

Published Time: 2026-11-03T02:48:07+00:00
先说结论：**DeepSeek Harness 能用，而且是我这两周试过的本地 agent 里，装完到跑通路径最短的一个。**
但它的坑不在功能上，在环境上。我用一台干净的 Ubuntu 22.04 从零装了一遍，踩了两个坑，其中一个会让你以为"软件装坏了"。

一句话：**DeepSeek Harness 不是模型，是跑模型的壳。**
模型（DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 之类）负责思考，Harness 负责把这些事接起来：读写文件、执行命令、维护任务计划、管理会话、管权限、管插件。
你可以把它理解成 IDE 里的"驾驶舱"：模型是发动机，Harness 是方向盘、油门和仪表盘。换个发动机还能继续开。

en.title: DeepSeek Harness hands-on: two commands to install, 632 lines of code written in 11 steps, all 3 tests green
en.summary:
DeepSeek Harness hands-on: installed with two commands, 632 lines of code written in 11 steps, all 3 tests green

Bottom line: DeepSeek Harness works, and among the local agents I’ve tried over the past two weeks, it has the shortest path from installation to a working run. Its pitfalls are in the environment, not the features. I installed it from scratch on a clean Ubuntu 22.04 and hit two snags, one of which can make you think the software is broken. What follows is the full process from installation to use. All figures come from real runs, and the screenshots were taken during actual server operations. In one sentence: DeepSeek Harness is not a model but a shell for running models. The model, such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, does the thinking, while Harness connects file reads and writes, command execution, task planning, session management, permissions, and plugins. Think of it as the cockpit in an IDE: the model is the engine, and Harness is the steering wheel, accelerator, and dashboard; you can swap the engine and keep driving. Version 0.2.1-rc.5 is a preview release, and the official notes explicitly warn of breaking changes.
en.reason: DeepSeek Harness preview 0.2.1-rc.5 installs on a clean Ubuntu 22.04 despite Node 22 and npm 11 blocking its install script, then an agent writes a 632-line Markdown-to-CSV tool in 11 steps with all 3 tests green.

en.title: DeepSeek goes down again — is DeepSeek V5 on the way?
en.summary:
DeepSeek Goes Down Again—Is DeepSeek V5 on the Way?
Published Time: 2026-11-04T10:07:05+00:00

DeepSeek has recently suffered slow responses and brief outages again, and these server-side fluctuations quickly sparked widespread discussion. Every system wobble fuels community speculation about a new version release. From identifiers spotted in the official evaluation code repository to supply-chain rumors that Huawei Ascend 950 may take on training workloads, clues about DeepSeek V5 are indeed accumulating. But looking objectively at the facts, these signs mostly reflect early engineering preparation and compute validation; there is still a clear time gap before an official launch.
## DeepSeek's servers are down again—is a new model coming?
DeepSeek has crashed yet again. Its web interface and API have seen connection timeouts and service degradation in multiple regions. On the 15th of last month, DeepSeek already had a server overload; less than a month later, DeepSeek going down has hit trending topics once more.
When other apps go down, most people just complain on social media about the poor experience. But with DeepSeek, reactions tend to take a sharp turn: Is the backend quietly canary-testing a model switch? Is the next-generation version about to launch?
As a heavy user who relies on it every day, I'd also love it to be a new model going live.
en.reason: DeepSeek's web and API endpoints again saw connection timeouts and service degradation, fueling V5 speculation over v5-open and v5-next identifiers in test code and Huawei Ascend 950 training rumors, though launch readiness depends on GitHub weight configs and open-platform interfaces.

en.title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 enables stateless HTTP mode by default, adds multi-turn request support
en.summary:
Microsoft has officially released MCP C# SDK 2.0, implementing the 2026-07-28 revision of the MCP specification. The release refactors the HTTP layer around a stateless design and adds support for multi-round trip requests (MRTR) and dynamic capability negotiation.

The initialize handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header are gone: protocol version and capability declarations now travel with each request. Streamable HTTP servers are stateless by default, and HTTP request headers are standardized to simplify infrastructure routing. Legacy clients degrade gracefully, while state-related configuration and the traditional SSE endpoint trigger explicit warning codes (MCP9006/MCP9004).
en.reason: Microsoft's MCP C# SDK 2.0 implements the MCP 2026-07-28 revision, defaults Streamable HTTP servers to stateless, drops the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header, adds multi-round-trip requests (MRTR), and flags legacy stateful or SSE setups with MCP9006/MCP9004 warnings.

en.title: Google releases ML Drift to accelerate on-device AI inference across GPUs
en.summary:
Google launches ML Drift, an open-source cross-platform GPU compute engine for on-device AI and machine learning inference.

Word count: 1,240 words
Reading time: about 4 minutes

ML Drift is Google's open-source cross-platform GPU inference engine, built specifically for on-device AI. It unifies OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU behind a single abstraction and powers the LiteRT runtime.

It supports 5D tensors, tensor-virtualizing shaders and extensible custom operators; it is deeply optimized for Arm, Intel and Qualcomm GPUs; and it provides an inference foundation that balances the stability of traditional ML with the peak performance demanded by generative AI.

Intended for edge AI engineers, on-device inference framework developers and builders of heterogeneous computing runtimes.

Google has released ML Drift, an open-source, cross-platform GPU compute engine designed for on-device AI and machine learning inference. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it abstracts away the complexity of different GPU hardware and low-level APIs, supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU.

ML Drift is the core GPU acceleration engine powering LiteRT
en.reason: Google open-sourced ML Drift, an Apache 2.0 cross-platform GPU inference engine for on-device AI that unifies OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU, powers LiteRT, and cuts memory overhead 12% versus llama.cpp and MLX LM.

en.title: DeepSeek Harness hands-on: two commands to install, 632 lines of code written in 11 steps, all 3 tests green
en.summary:
DeepSeek Harness hands-on: installed with two commands, 632 lines of code written in 11 steps, all 3 tests green

Bottom line: DeepSeek Harness works, and among the local agents I’ve tried over the past two weeks, it has the shortest path from installation to a working run. Its pitfalls are in the environment, not the features. I installed it from scratch on a clean Ubuntu 22.04 and hit two snags, one of which can make you think the software is broken. What follows is the full process from installation to use. All figures come from real runs, and the screenshots were taken during actual server operations. In one sentence: DeepSeek Harness is not a model but a shell for running models. The model, such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, does the thinking, while Harness connects file reads and writes, command execution, task planning, session management, permissions, and plugins. Think of it as the cockpit in an IDE: the model is the engine, and Harness is the steering wheel, accelerator, and dashboard; you can swap the engine and keep driving. Version 0.2.1-rc.5 is a preview release, and the official notes explicitly warn of breaking changes.
en.reason: DeepSeek Harness preview 0.2.1-rc.5 installs on a clean Ubuntu 22.04 despite Node 22 and npm 11 blocking its install script, then an agent writes a 632-line Markdown-to-CSV tool in 11 steps with all 3 tests green.

en.title: DeepSeek goes down again — is DeepSeek V5 on the way?
en.summary:
DeepSeek Goes Down Again—Is DeepSeek V5 on the Way?
Published Time: 2026-11-04T10:07:05+00:00

DeepSeek has recently suffered slow responses and brief outages again, and these server-side fluctuations quickly sparked widespread discussion. Every system wobble fuels community speculation about a new version release. From identifiers spotted in the official evaluation code repository to supply-chain rumors that Huawei Ascend 950 may take on training workloads, clues about DeepSeek V5 are indeed accumulating. But looking objectively at the facts, these signs mostly reflect early engineering preparation and compute validation; there is still a clear time gap before an official launch.
## DeepSeek's servers are down again—is a new model coming?
DeepSeek has crashed yet again. Its web interface and API have seen connection timeouts and service degradation in multiple regions. On the 15th of last month, DeepSeek already had a server overload; less than a month later, DeepSeek going down has hit trending topics once more.
When other apps go down, most people just complain on social media about the poor experience. But with DeepSeek, reactions tend to take a sharp turn: Is the backend quietly canary-testing a model switch? Is the next-generation version about to launch?
As a heavy user who relies on it every day, I'd also love it to be a new model going live.
en.reason: DeepSeek's web and API endpoints again saw connection timeouts and service degradation, fueling V5 speculation over v5-open and v5-next identifiers in test code and Huawei Ascend 950 training rumors, though launch readiness depends on GitHub weight configs and open-platform interfaces.
